 Oral Judgment

1. This appeal is filed by the claimant against the judgment and award dated 11.01.2022 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T. Kalaburagi, [for short 'Tribunal'] in MVC No.974/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The injured claimant aged 58 years, met with an accident on 24.09.2016 and sustained grievous injuries.
Hence, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-.

The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record, awarded the compensation of Rs.3,08,517/- with interest at 6% per NC: 2025:KHC-K:6774 HC-KAR annum from the date of petition till realization and directed respondent-Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
Aggrieved by the said award, the appellant-claimant has preferred this appeal.

3. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material available on record.
4.
The main contention of the appellant is that the Tribunal has awarded meagre compensation under all heads and no award is granted for future medical expenses.
It is contended that claimant sustained fracture of lower ends of both radius with internal fixation of plate and screws in situ and the injuries are grievous in nature.
It is also contended that the Tribunal discarded the evidence of PW2 - Doctor in regard to disability at 46% and has considered at just 16% only.

It is further contended that the Tribunal erred in considering the income of appellant at just Rs.8,750/- instead of Rs.15,000/- per month and thus, requested for enhancing the compensation in his favour.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and needs no interference.
6. Admittedly as per Ex.P6 - Wound Certificate the claimant has sustained grievous injuries and as per Ex.P8 - Disability Certificate, the Doctor - PW2, has assessed 46% disability to the whole body.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained and the treatment undergone, the Tribunal has considered the functional disability at 16% which needs no interference.
7. Further, though, the claimant states that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, he has not produced any document to prove the same.

As the accident is of the year 2016, the Tribunal has considered the notional income at Rs.8,750/- per month as per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which is just and proper.
At the time of accident, the claimant was aged 56 years and appropriate multiplier NC: 2025:KHC-K:6774 HC-KAR applicable to his age group is '9'.
Considering all these relevant factors, the Tribunal has rightly awarded Rs.1,51,200/- towards loss of future earning capacity, which needs no interference.
8. The claimant was admitted in the hospital for 5 days.

Considering the period of hospitalization,
nature of injuries and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to award an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.35,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
9. Admittedly, the claimant was having internal fixation of plate and screws.
Hence, for removal of the same, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.15,000/- towards future medical expenses.

10. Further, due to injuries the claimant might not have attended any work atleast for a period of 4 months, hence, this Court finds it reasonable to award Rs.35,000/-
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6774 HC-KAR for loss of income during laid up period.
However, the compensation of Rs.56,067/- awarded by the Tribunal for medical expenses, needs no interference.

11. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is modified as under:
Sl. Heads Award by the Award by this No. Tribunal Court 1 Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/- Rs.50,000/- 2

Medical Expenses Rs.56,067/- Rs.56,067/- 3 Loss of future Rs.1,51,200/- Rs.1,51,200/-
earning capacity 4 Transportation, Rs.20,000/- Rs.30,000/-
extra nourishment and attendant charges 5 Loss of amenities Rs.15,000/- Rs.35,000/- 6 Loss of income Rs.26,250/- Rs.35,000/-
during laid up period 7

Future medical -- Rs.15,000/-

13. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
( ii) The claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.63,750/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
(iii) Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount along with interest within one month from the date of this judgment.
